patch_resolves_note: The fixed original resolves the reproduced 6-byte crash by returning at the FILE_REGEX guard before any window or memchr state is derived from `offset = 12`. The adjacent `size13_append7_zeros` perturbation is used only to witness the guarded root obligation with the protected memchr event present; that witness later trips a separate allocator failure after the verified sink event executes.

root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `nbytes >= offset` before the FILE_REGEX arm uses `offset`
root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before the FILE_REGEX arm may derive its search window from `offset`, it must establish `nbytes >= offset` so the newline scan stays within the live input buffer.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the regex newline scan even though `nbytes = 6` and `offset = 12`. The fixed original guards the stock PoC at the same site, and the closest source-grounded witness `size13_append7_zeros` executes the protected memchr event with the predicate true (`13 >= 12`).
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original trace records `regex_guard.nbytes=6`, `regex_guard.offset=12`, and still reaches `regex_memchr_sink`. The fixed original is guarded at the same event, and the fixed `size13_append7_zeros` trace records `nbytes=13 >= offset=12` while `regex_memchr_sink` executes.

nodes.description: At the first FILE_REGEX newline scan, `memchr` receives a 320-byte search span whose initialized prefix is only 5 bytes on the crashing original path.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original assertion trace records `regex_memchr_sink.scan_remaining_bytes=320 > regex_memchr_sink.scan_initialized_prefix_len=5`.

nodes.description: At regex window setup, `buf = s + offset` starts beyond the logical end of the 6-byte witness, so the later scan begins outside the live input.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original assertion trace records `regex_window.window_start_ptr > regex_window.input_end_ptr`.

edges.relation: The same `offset` value compared at the missing guard is reused unchanged when `buf = s + offset` builds the regex search window.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `regex_guard.offset == regex_window.offset == 12`; the fixed `size13_append7_zeros` witness preserves the same equality.

edges.relation: The out-of-range `buf` pointer computed for the regex window is the same start pointer consumed as `b` by the first memchr scan.
edges.evidence: Both the vulnerable original and the fixed `size13_append7_zeros` witness record `regex_window.window_start_ptr == regex_memchr_sink.scan_start_ptr`.
